newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela 6-month TEM yields rise to 16.48 pct.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela 6-month TEM yields rise to 16.48 pct.

text.p: Yields on Venezuelan benchmark six-month TEMs rose 112 basis points to 16.48 percent in Wednesday's auction, according to a Reuters calculation using the Central Bank formula.
The Central Bank said it sold 80 billion bolivars of 180-day "monetary stabilization", or TEM, bills at a price of 99.48 pct down from 99.66 last week, in its weekly auction.
The bills carried a 15.36 percent coupon. At last week's auctions, six-month notes yielded 14.63 percent.
The bank also sold 10 billion bolivars of 269-day notes with a 15.65 percent coupon at a price of 96.54 percent.
For 358-day notes carrying a 15.95 percent coupon, the bank sold 10 billion bolivars at an average price of 94.89 percent.
Yields on these notes dropped 105 basis points to 21.01 percent for the 268-day bills, and 184 basis points to 22.22 percent for the 358-day TEMs.
The weekly TEM bill auctions are the Central Bank's main tool of monetary policy, used to restrict liquidity and establish a benchmark for wider interest rates.
